title: Homily XXVI
subtitle: Matthew 8:5
author: chrysostom
excerpt: The leper came unto Him “when He was come down from the mountain,” but this centurion, “when He was entered into Capernaum.” Wherefore then did neither the one…

footnotes.2: Luke vii. 2. [R.V., “and” at the point of death; κα in the citation means “and,” not “even.”—R.]
footnotes.4: δι τν ναντων τ νντια. The argument seems to require τ ατ, “the same things by opposite means:” but no ms. authority appears for such a change.
footnotes.8: [R.V., “only say the word,” “Gr. with a word.” Chrysostom varies from the order, placing “only” last.—R.]
footnotes.13: Matt. viii. 10. [The reading of the received text is found here. Comp. R.V. margin for the reading of the Vatican ms., accepted by Augustin.—R.]
footnotes.18: Matt. viii. 10. Comp. στραφες, is taken from the latter passage.—R.]
footnotes.19: Matt. viii. 11, 12. [For “with” Chrysostom substitutes “in the bosom of” (ε το κλπου), commenting upon the term below (sec. 5). There is no authority for this reading, so far as now known.—R.]
footnotes.31: Matt. vi. 33. [Comp. Hom. XXII. 4, p.148, on the reading “kingdom of heaven.”—R.]
footnotes.34: [Both terms were current in Jewish theological language; but it is implied in the argument that “Abraham’s bosom” was not so well known, or so definitely apprehended.—R.]
footnotes.44: Both these sects ascribed the Old Testament to an evil principle, and argued against it from such cases as this of David. Of Marcion, see St. Iren. i. 29, iv. 45. Of Manes, St. Aug. contra Faustum. xxii. 5, 66. [Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, first series, vol. iv. p. 297.]
